meta.title: AGAP SOS Emergency Flow — Data Flow Reference
meta.description: Documents every table, field, and relationship touched during a citizen SOS trigger. Covers the 4-step capture sequence: SOS Button → Location → What's Happening → Add More Details.
architecturalRules: Incident record is persisted to PostgreSQL BEFORE any background job
Optional fields (GPS, photo, medical) must NEVER block emergency submission
Reporter and patient are always separate records
Unknown patient is fully valid — never blocks dispatch
Offline retries are idempotent — same client_event_id = same incident, never a duplicate

flow.name: SOS Button Pressed
flow.trigger: Citizen taps the SOS button in mobile/app/emergency/sos.tsx
flow.description: The moment the button is pressed, a client_event_id (UUID) is generated on-device as the idempotency key. The app simultaneously fires the data path (HTTPS) and the SMS path (Textbee). If both fail, the event is saved to the local offline queue.
sequence: 1c. Attempt SMS via Textbee in parallel (payload < 160 chars)
1d. If both fail → save to offline_event_queue
1e. On reconnect → flush queue using original client_event_id

alert_triggers.purpose: Raw log of every trigger event before an Incident is confirmed

incident_id.notes: FK to Incident; linked after Incident is created

user_id.notes: Nullable — guest reporters have no user_id

client_event_id.notes: UNIQUE — idempotency key generated on-device at trigger time

latitude.notes: Best-available at trigger moment; may be refined later

was_cancelled.notes: Set to true if user cancels within deadline

Incident.purpose: Central business object — created synchronously, before any background job

id.notes: Internal PK; never exposed in API

public_reference.notes: e.g. INC-2026-001234 — this is what citizens and dispatchers see

client_event_id.notes: UNIQUE — links Incident back to alert_triggers; enables dedup

priority.notes: Default MEDIUM; MOD-24 may upgrade based on category/signals

status.notes: Always starts at SUBMITTED on citizen trigger

river_level_meters.notes: Only relevant for FLOOD category; Bocaue River critical = 11.50m

IncidentReporter.purpose: Who pressed the button — always separate from the patient record

user_id.notes: Nullable — guest reporters have no AGAP account

is_guest.notes: true if user is unauthenticated bystander

reporter_name.notes: Optional; populated from profile for registered users

contact_callback.notes: Alternative callback number provided at trigger time

offline_event_queue.purpose: Local queue when both data + SMS paths fail; flushed on reconnect
offline_event_queue.condition: Only written if HTTPS POST and SMS both fail (connectivity loss in flood zones, etc.)

client_event_id.notes: UNIQUE — same key as alert_triggers; prevents double-processing

payload.notes: Full incident payload exactly as it would have been sent

device_info.notes: OS, connectivity state at queue time

queued_at_device.notes: When the event was queued on-device (may differ from server received_at)

received_at_server.notes: When the server received the flushed event

processed_at.notes: When the backend processed the queued event

flow.name: Getting Your Location
flow.trigger: Expo Location API captures GPS coordinates; backend reverse-geocodes to barangay/address
flow.description: GPS capture happens in parallel with SOS trigger. The coordinates are attached to the Incident as incident_locations. If GPS is unavailable, the Incident is still submitted — location is optional and must never block dispatch.
flow.optionalNote: Missing GPS must never block Incident creation or dispatch (Architectural Rule #5)

incident_locations.purpose: The pinned GPS location of the emergency — one record per Incident

incident_id.notes: UNIQUE FK to Incident — one location per incident

point.notes: Derived from lat/lng; enables ST_DWithin proximity queries

barangay.notes: Critical for Bocaue barangay-level dispatch routing

location_history.purpose: Ongoing location breadcrumbs for live tracking (MOD-13) — written continuously after initial capture

flow.name: What's Happening
flow.trigger: Citizen selects emergency category and fills in situation details in mobile/app/emergency/incident-details.tsx
flow.description: The citizen selects an emergency category and provides additional context. These fields update the Incident record and create an incident_details child record. Patient information is captured separately in incident_patients — patient identity is never assumed from the reporter.

Incident.purpose: Top-level fields updated at this step

number_of_patients.notes: Citizen's estimate of number of people needing help

river_level_meters.notes: Only shown for FLOOD category; Bocaue River critical = 11.50m

incident_details.purpose: Extended incident-specific detail fields — one-to-one with Incident

incident_id.notes: UNIQUE FK — one details record per incident

people_affected.notes: Default 1; total people in area affected (may be > patients)

water_level_note.notes: Narrative water level description for FLOOD category

additional_notes.notes: Any other details the citizen provides

first_aid_guide_id.notes: FK to first_aid_guides — system links a relevant guide based on category

incident_patients.purpose: Patient record(s) — always kept separate from IncidentReporter
incident_patients.criticalRule: Reporter ≠ Patient — NEVER auto-link the reporter as a patient. Unknown patient is valid and must never block dispatch.

is_reporter.notes: true only if citizen explicitly indicates they are the patient

is_unknown.notes: true when patient identity cannot be determined — fully valid state

user_id.notes: Only populated if patient is a known AGAP user who consents; never auto-linked

medical_profile_id.notes: FK to MedicalProfile — requires separate ConsentRecord; missing never blocks dispatch

scene_assessment_notes.notes: Filled by responder on-scene, not by citizen

vitals_at_scene.notes: Blood pressure, pulse, etc. — filled on-scene

first_aid_guides.purpose: Read-only lookup — system surfaces relevant first aid content to citizen while waiting for responders
first_aid_guides.operation: READ only — citizen flow never writes to this table

steps.notes: Ordered step array for display in mobile app

flow.name: Add More Details (Photo Attachment)
flow.trigger: Citizen optionally attaches a photo using Expo Camera or Image Picker in mobile/app/emergency/photo.tsx
flow.description: Photos are uploaded to object storage. The IncidentAttachment record links the stored file back to the Incident. Uploading a photo is entirely optional — its absence never delays or blocks the incident.
flow.optionalNote: Photo upload must never block Incident creation or dispatch (Architectural Rule #5)

IncidentAttachment.purpose: Metadata record for each file attached to the incident — actual binary stored in object storage

incident_id.notes: FK to Incident; multiple attachments allowed per incident

file_type.notes: MIME type, e.g. image/jpeg, image/png, video/mp4

storage_key.notes: Path within the bucket — never expose to public directly

storage_url.notes: Presigned URL for authorized access; regenerated on each download request

is_processed.notes: true after server-side processing (virus scan, thumbnail generation)

crossCuttingTables.description: Tables written to in the background after the SOS flow completes — not part of the 4-step citizen capture sequence but triggered by it

IncidentEvent.purpose: Immutable status transition log — one record per status change
IncidentEvent.trigger: Written every time Incident.status changes (SUBMITTED → RECEIVED → ACKNOWLEDGED etc.)

AuditLog.purpose: Immutable audit trail for all consequential actions — no UPDATE or DELETE ever
AuditLog.trigger: Written on every CREATE, STATUS_CHANGE, and sensitive data access

incident_id.notes: Always linked when action is incident-related

Notification.purpose: Tracks all outbound push and SMS notifications triggered by the incident
Notification.trigger: Background job (BullMQ) queued after Incident creation
Notification.reliabilityRule: A failed notification must NEVER delete or cancel the Incident

sms_payload.notes: Always <= 160 chars for single-segment SMS delivery

tableRelationshipSummary.description: Primary key relationships across the SOS flow

relationships.notes: Read-only lookup; citizen never writes here

fieldSourceLegend.mobile: Sent by the Expo mobile app at trigger time
fieldSourceLegend.JWT: Extracted from the Bearer token in the Authorization header
fieldSourceLegend.server-generated: Created by the NestJS backend (UUID, timestamps, etc.)
fieldSourceLegend.server (reverse geocoding): Populated asynchronously via map provider after record creation
fieldSourceLegend.Expo Location: Captured by the expo-location library from device GPS/network
fieldSourceLegend.mobile (user selection): Citizen explicitly chose from a UI picker
fieldSourceLegend.mobile (user input): Citizen typed a free-text or numeric value
fieldSourceLegend.mobile (multi-select): Citizen selected one or more options from a list
fieldSourceLegend.responder (MOD-37): Filled by responder on-scene — not part of citizen SOS flow
